text:
Amadeus Lombardi is 17 games into his NHL career and still waiting for the first goal. That's the kind of stat that sticks to a rookie, but it isn't a fair read of his play. He's had 2.8 expected goals of chances and 25 shots, and goals usually follow looks like those.

The 23-year-old from Newmarket, Ontario was a fourth-round pick by Detroit in 2022 and scored 42 points in 47 AHL games for Grand Rapids last season before landing in New Jersey. He plays about 11 minutes a night and has 4 assists. His speed is real (his skating bursts over 20 mph rank in the top 7% of the league), and with him on ice at five on five the Devils take about 56% of shot attempts.

The catch is the chance quality: expected goals with him on the ice are an even split, and the Devils are about eight points better without him. His most recent game in our data was Nov. 10 in Winnipeg, and he didn't play the two wins over Washington. Earning back steady minutes, and that first goal, is his story right now.
